annotations.title: Check the card a link shows when shared on X, Facebook, LinkedIn and chat apps

description: Use when the user asks how a link will look when shared, why a shared link shows no image or the wrong title, or wants a page checked before a launch post (signals: "link preview", "og:image not showing", "Twitter card", "X card", "social card", "share image", "unfurl", "Open Graph", "LinkedIn preview is blank", "after deploying the landing page"). Fetches the public page the way a link crawler does (following redirects, no JavaScript), reads the og: and twitter: tags with X's documented fallbacks (twitter:* then og:*, last twitter:card wins), downloads the og:image and twitter:image and reads their real pixel size, format and file size from the bytes, and checks robots.txt for Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit on the page and the image. Returns the card X, Facebook, LinkedIn and chat apps will build, every problem with severity and fix (relative or http image URL, image that is really an HTML page, SVG or AVIF, below X's 300x157 / Facebook's 200x200 / LinkedIn's 1200x627, over 5 MB, 2:1 crop of a square logo, tags added by JavaScript, tags past Facebook's first 1 MB, title over X's 70 characters, missing twitter:card, robots.txt blocks), and a paste-ready <meta> block. Rules come from the platforms' docs, with the check date. Example: {"url":"https://example.com/launch"}. Limits: public http/https pages on ports 80 and 443 (localhost and unpublished pages go through postcard_check_preview_tags); platforms cache cards (X for about 7 days), so a fixed page can still show the old card until rescraped; sites that serve different HTML to real crawlers by User-Agent can differ.

url.description: The page address people will share, for example "https://example.com/blog/launch".
